rawInput.answer:
Parameters are captured in two phases in tree.go, both governed by findWildcard (tree.go:253).

**Registration (insertChild, tree.go:288):** When a route like `/user/:name` is inserted, findWildcard locates the `:name` segment. insertChild splits the path so the prefix before the colon becomes the parent node's path, then creates a new child node with `nType: param` and `path: ":name"` (colon retained), and sets the parent's `wildChild = true`. addChild (tree.go:71) guarantees this wildcard child is always kept last in the children slice, so static children are always tried first during matching. If more path follows the param (e.g. `/user/:name/books`), a further static child is chained after it; if not, handlers are attached directly to the param node.

**Matching (getValue, tree.go:418):** While walking the tree, static children are tried first by matching `n.indices` against the next path byte. If none match and `n.wildChild` is true, the walker jumps to `n.children[len(n.children)-1]` (the wildcard child) and increments `globalParamsCount`. For `nType == param`, it scans forward from the current position until it hits `/` or the end of the path to find the parameter's value boundary (`path[:end]`), optionally URL-unescapes it, and appends `Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: val}` to the shared `Params` slice — `n.path[1:]` strips the leading `:` to get the bare name (e.g. `"name"`). If the path continues past `end`, matching recurses into the child after the `/`; otherwise handlers are returned if present.

Catch-all wildcards (`*filepath`) work similarly but consume the entire remaining path as the value and use `n.path[2:]` as the key (stripping the leading `/*`).

The `Params` slice itself is preallocated per-request in Engine.allocateContext (gin.go:252) with capacity `engine.maxParams`, which is computed at registration time via countParams (tree.go:80, counts `:` and `*` occurrences) and tracked as the max across all registered routes (gin.go addRoute). This avoids heap allocation during matching — the slice is reused from the pool and just re-sliced/appended into on each request.

report.answer:
Parameters are captured in two phases in tree.go, both governed by findWildcard (tree.go:253).

**Registration (insertChild, tree.go:288):** When a route like `/user/:name` is inserted, findWildcard locates the `:name` segment. insertChild splits the path so the prefix before the colon becomes the parent node's path, then creates a new child node with `nType: param` and `path: ":name"` (colon retained), and sets the parent's `wildChild = true`. addChild (tree.go:71) guarantees this wildcard child is always kept last in the children slice, so static children are always tried first during matching. If more path follows the param (e.g. `/user/:name/books`), a further static child is chained after it; if not, handlers are attached directly to the param node.

**Matching (getValue, tree.go:418):** While walking the tree, static children are tried first by matching `n.indices` against the next path byte. If none match and `n.wildChild` is true, the walker jumps to `n.children[len(n.children)-1]` (the wildcard child) and increments `globalParamsCount`. For `nType == param`, it scans forward from the current position until it hits `/` or the end of the path to find the parameter's value boundary (`path[:end]`), optionally URL-unescapes it, and appends `Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: val}` to the shared `Params` slice — `n.path[1:]` strips the leading `:` to get the bare name (e.g. `"name"`). If the path continues past `end`, matching recurses into the child after the `/`; otherwise handlers are returned if present.

Catch-all wildcards (`*filepath`) work similarly but consume the entire remaining path as the value and use `n.path[2:]` as the key (stripping the leading `/*`).

The `Params` slice itself is preallocated per-request in Engine.allocateContext (gin.go:252) with capacity `engine.maxParams`, which is computed at registration time via countParams (tree.go:80, counts `:` and `*` occurrences) and tracked as the max across all registered routes (gin.go addRoute). This avoids heap allocation during matching — the slice is reused from the pool and just re-sliced/appended into on each request.
